featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are hunting for genuine, no-fuss Konkani and Malvani food in Mumbai, your search ends at Konkan Swad in Jogeshwari West. This restaurant is truly a hidden gem, offering an unparalleled taste of the coast that transports you straight to the shores of Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg. It's the kind of place you visit when you crave authentic, home-style seafood and fiery curries.
The highlight here is, without a doubt, the seafood. The fish is always incredibly fresh—a mandatory requirement for any great coastal establishment. I highly recommend starting with the Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck) or the Surmai Fry. The coating is perfectly crisp, and the marinade is a flawless blend of chili, turmeric, and spice. For the main course, the Prawn Curry Thali is a masterpiece; rich, coconut-based gravy that pairs perfectly with the soft, fluffy Vade (puri made from rice and lentil flour). If you prefer meat, the Chicken Malvani Thali is equally robust and satisfying.
Beyond the main courses, don't miss out on the incredible Solkadhi. This kokam-based digestive drink is creamy, tangy, and absolutely essential for cooling the palate after the spicy Konkani flavors. It’s one of the best I've had outside of a Konkani home.
The ambiance is simple, clean, and unpretentious, allowing the focus to remain solely on the food, as it should be. The staff is warm, helpful, and eager to offer recommendations, making the entire dining experience feel incredibly homely. If you love coastal flavors, fresh fish, and authentic Malvani spices, Konkan Swad is a must-visit destination in Jogeshwari. Highly, highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place has a G+2 seating arrangement—non-AC on the ground floor and AC seating on the first and second floors. Seating is decent.

Unlike many traditional bars, no complimentary chakna is served here. Alcohol prices felt on the higher side, and the 180 ml vodka was served from a larger container instead of a sealed bottle, which was a bit disappointing. Mixers were limited to Coke and Sprite only. Initially, staff said outside mixers would be charged extra, but after speaking to the manager, they allowed to buy it from outside without any charge.

Service was decent but not very attentive, especially towards regular or light drinkers—attention seemed more focused on heavy customers.

Coming to food: Apple Chicken was good, and the green kokani/malvani-style kairi chutney served with it was unique and delicious. We ordered Chicken Thali (₹300) and Mutton Thali (₹430). Quantity felt slightly less for the price—total four pieces (two gravy, two fry). Taste-wise, chicken and mutton gravies and fries had almost the same masala, which reduced variety.

Ambience is decent overall, but the washroom ceiling is quite low, which can be uncomfortable for tall people.

Overall, a decent experience—good chutney and some dishes stand out, but quantity, attention to service, and a few basic facilities can definitely improve.

We ordered the Bangda Thali and Prawns Thali, and both were absolutely delicious. The Prawns Fry served as a starter was perfectly spiced and crispy, while the Solkadi was refreshing and authentic.

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!

featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I got to know about this place through YouTube channel Curly Tales, that discusses the favourite food of various celebrities around the country. This place was heavily recommended over the channel by Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, hence making it easier in terms of choosing the place.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Keep up the good work.

​I visited The Fisherman’s Kitchen on a Friday evening with high expectations, given the name and the positive reviews. While the atmosphere is family-friendly and the location is convenient (right below Bangur Nagar Metro with valet parking), the food was a mixed bag.
​The Standouts: The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was easily the highlight—the fish was incredibly fresh and perfectly cooked (4.5/5). Pairing the remaining gravy with Neer Dosa was the best part of the meal.
​The Letdowns: Unfortunately, the Prawns Tandoori didn't taste fresh (2.5/5), and the Crab Soup was watery with very little meat. The Kadipatta Chicken was also quite average; the chicken felt a bit tough and lacked that punchy Mangalorean flavor I was looking for.
​The Verdict:
​Ambience & Service: 3.5/5
​Alcohol Variety: 4/5
Food: 3/5
​Value for Money: 3/5
It’s a decent place for a family outing, and perhaps I caught them on an off-night, but for a seafood specialty restaurant, I expected more consistency in freshness.

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.
